## 2. Import CVFS data: Labour Outmigration, Agricultural Productivity and Food Security, Nepal, 2015-2017 
```{r}
# A. Load data
github_remittance_url <- paste0(
  "https://github.com/ellenthickman/687Project/raw/",
  "refs/heads/main/36755-0001-Data.rda"
)

temp_env <- new.env()
loaded_names <- load(url(github_remittance_url), envir = temp_env)

loaded_names
remit_w <- temp_env[[loaded_names[1]]]

# B. Select variables
tv_prefixes <- c(
  "A10_", "B11C_", "B12C_", "B13C_",
  "B14C_", "B15C_", "B16B_", "B17_1B_", "B17_2B_",
  "B17_3B_", "B17_4B_", "B17_5B_", "B17_6B_",
  "B17_7B_", "C18_", "C19_", "C20_", "D30B_", "D31B_", "C21_", "REM"
)

remit_w <- remit_w |>
  select(HHID, ETHNICITY,  starts_with(tv_prefixes) & !ends_with("63")) # Excluding year 2063 due to missing data in gfp indicator

# C. Transform from wide to long
remit_l <- remit_w |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = matches(
      paste0(
        "^(",
        paste(tv_prefixes, collapse = "|"),
        ")(64|65|66|67|68|69|70|71|72)$" 
      )
    ),
    names_to = c(".value", "year"),
    names_pattern = "^(.*?)(64|65|66|67|68|69|70|71|72)$",
    names_transform = list(year = as.integer)
  )
```
## 3. Clean Data
```{r}
# A. Create a gross farm product
## i. Set variable list
gfp_vars <- c("B11C_", # Rice (KG)
              "B12C_", # Maize (KG)
              "B13C_", # Wheat (KG)
              "B14C_", # Mustard (KG)
              "B15C_", # Red Lentil (KG)
              "B16B_", # Vegetable
              "B17_1B_", # Buckwheat
              "B17_2B_", # Finger millet
              "B17_3B_", # Sesame
              "B17_4B_", # Kidney bean
              "B17_5B_", # Pea/gram
              "B17_6B_", # Cowpea/bean
              "B17_7B_", # Other crops
              "D30B_", # Poultry production
              "D31B_") # Other farming production

## ii. Mutate to generate gfp indicator
remit_l <- remit_l |>
  mutate(
    across(
      any_of(gfp_vars),
      ~ as.numeric(as.character(.x))
    ),
    gfp = rowSums(across(any_of(gfp_vars)), na.rm = TRUE)
  )

## iii. Drop extraneous variables 
remit_l <- remit_l |>
  select(-any_of(gfp_vars))
```

```{r}
# B. Rename variables
remit_l <- remit_l |>
  rename(
    rem = REM,
    hired_lab = C21_,
    land_owned = A10_,
    hhid = HHID,
    ethnic = ETHNICITY,
    tractor_time = C18_,
    thresher_used = C19_,
    motor_used = C20_
  )
```

```{r}
# C. Create farm technology indicator
remit_l <- remit_l |>
  mutate(
    tractor_used = case_when(
      tractor_time == 0 ~ 0,
      tractor_time > 0 & tractor_time <= 6600 ~ 1,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_),
    across(c(thresher_used, motor_used),
           ~ case_when(
             as.character(.x) %in% c("(0) No" , "0")  ~ 0,
             as.character(.x) %in% c("(1) Yes", "1")  ~ 1,
             TRUE ~ NA_real_)),
    farm_tech = tractor_used + thresher_used + motor_used)
```

```{r}
# D. Transform land owned from a time variant to a time invariant variable
# i. Summary of land owned by year
remit_l |>
  group_by(year) |>
  summarise(
    Min = min(land_owned, na.rm = TRUE),
    Q1 = quantile(land_owned, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
    Median = median(land_owned, na.rm = TRUE),
    Mean = mean(land_owned, na.rm = TRUE),
    Q3 = quantile(land_owned, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),
    Max = max(land_owned, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) round(x, 2))) |>
  kable(caption = "Summary of land owned by year (Katha)")

## ii. View who has changed in land ownership over the years
remit_l |>
  group_by(hhid) |>
  summarize(distinct_values = n_distinct(land_owned, na.rm = TRUE)) |>
  count(distinct_values)

tv_land <- remit_l |>
  group_by(hhid) |>
  filter(n_distinct(land_owned, na.rm = TRUE) > 1) |>
  ungroup(); tv_land

land_variance <- remit_l |>
  group_by(hhid) |>
  filter(n_distinct(land_owned, na.rm = TRUE) > 1) |> # Optional: keep to only look at varying households
  summarize(
    land_var = var(land_owned, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ); land_variance

## iii. Create an average
remit_l <- remit_l |>
    group_by(hhid) |>
  mutate(
    land_avg = mean(land_owned, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) |>
  ungroup()
```
We have 571 (25%) of households whose landownership changes across the 9 years. Does it change drastically? Do we take the starting value, end value, or average?

### G. Check missing values vs 0 sales
```{r}
raw_data <- temp_env[[loaded_names[1]]]

check_vars <- c(
  "B11C_", "B12C_", "B13C_", "B14C_", "B15C_",
  "B16B_",
  "B17_1B_", "B17_2B_", "B17_3B_", "B17_4B_",
  "B17_5B_", "B17_6B_", "B17_7B_",
  "D30B_", "D31B_"
)

missing_check <- lapply(63:72, function(y) {

  column_names <- paste0(check_vars, y)
  components <- raw_data[, column_names, drop = FALSE]

  stopifnot(all(vapply(components, is.numeric, logical(1))))

  # Number of nonmissing components in each household-year
  n_observed <- rowSums(!is.na(components))

  # Reproduce the original calculation ONLY to diagnose missingness
  original_sum <- rowSums(components, na.rm = TRUE)

  data.frame(
    year = 2000 + y,
    total = nrow(components),
    all_missing = sum(n_observed == 0),
    partially_missing = sum(
      n_observed > 0 & n_observed < length(check_vars)
    ),
    complete = sum(n_observed == length(check_vars)),
    all_missing_but_sum_zero = sum(
      n_observed == 0 & original_sum == 0
    )
  )
})

missing_check <- bind_rows(missing_check)

kable(
  missing_check,
  caption = "Missingness in the original GFP components"
)
```

## 6. Running Models
### A. Plots
These models are preliminary. The current GFP composite mixes kilograms
and rupees.
```{r}
library(nlme)
library(dplyr)
library(knitr)
library(ggplot2)
# Retrieve original data without modifying remit_l
model_raw <- temp_env[[loaded_names[1]]]

component_names <- c(
  "B11C_", "B12C_", "B13C_", "B14C_", "B15C_",
  "B16B_",
  "B17_1B_", "B17_2B_", "B17_3B_", "B17_4B_",
  "B17_5B_", "B17_6B_", "B17_7B_",
  "D30B_", "D31B_"
)

# Count available components in each household-year
component_counts <- bind_rows(
  lapply(64:72, function(y) {

    components <- model_raw[
      , paste0(component_names, y),
      drop = FALSE
    ]

    tibble(
      hhid = model_raw$HHID,
      year = y,
      n_components = rowSums(!is.na(components))
    )
  })
)

stopifnot(
  !anyDuplicated(component_counts[c("hhid", "year")]),
  !anyDuplicated(remit_l[c("hhid", "year")])
)

# Create a separate dataset for Section 6
analysis_data <- remit_l |>
  left_join(
    component_counts,
    by = c("hhid", "year")
  ) |>
  mutate(
    # Prevent all-missing components from becoming a measured zero
    gfp_preview = if_else(
      n_components > 0,
      gfp,
      NA_real_
    ),
    year_bs = 2000L + year,
    time = as.integer(year - 64),
    wave = as.integer(year - 63),
    year_f = factor(year_bs),
    hhid = factor(hhid),
    ethnic = factor(ethnic),

    log_gfp = log1p(gfp_preview),
    log_rem = log1p(rem),
    log_labor = log1p(hired_lab),
    log_land = log1p(land_avg)
  ) |>
  arrange(hhid, wave)

stopifnot(!anyNA(analysis_data$n_components))

analysis_data |>
  group_by(year_bs) |>
  summarise(
    total = n(),
    all_components_missing = sum(n_components == 0),
    partially_observed = sum(
      n_components > 0 & n_components < 15
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  kable(
    caption = "Availability of original GFP components"
  )
```
```{r}
gfp_rebuilt <- bind_rows(
  lapply(64:72, function(y) {

    components <- model_raw[
      , paste0(component_names, y),
      drop = FALSE
    ]

    stopifnot(
      ncol(components) == 15,
      all(vapply(components, is.numeric, logical(1)))
    )

    n_available <- rowSums(!is.na(components))
    total <- rowSums(components, na.rm = TRUE)

    # Complete absence cannot be regarded as zero
    total[n_available == 0] <- NA_real_

    tibble(
      hhid = as.character(model_raw$HHID),
      year = y,
      gfp_rebuilt = total
    )
  })
)

analysis_data <- analysis_data |>
  mutate(hhid = as.character(hhid)) |>
  select(-any_of("gfp_rebuilt")) |>
  left_join(
    gfp_rebuilt,
    by = c("hhid", "year")
  ) |>
  mutate(
    gfp_preview = gfp_rebuilt,
    log_gfp = log1p(gfp_preview),
    hhid = factor(hhid)
  )

summary(analysis_data$gfp_preview)
summary(analysis_data$log_gfp)

stopifnot(
  any(analysis_data$gfp_preview > 0, na.rm = TRUE)
)
```

#### i. GFP by HH
Each household contributes one mean across its available years.
```{r}

    mean_log_gfp = if (all(is.na(log_gfp))) {

      mean(log_gfp, na.rm = TRUE)

hh_summary |>

```

#### iii. GFP by HH and year
```{r}
set.seed(687)

eligible_households <- analysis_data |>
  group_by(hhid) |>
  summarise(
    n_available = sum(is.finite(log_gfp)),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  filter(n_available >= 2) |>
  pull(hhid) |>
  as.character()

selected_households <- sample(
  eligible_households,
  size = min(20, length(eligible_households))
)

trajectory_data <- analysis_data |>
  filter(as.character(hhid) %in% selected_households)

trajectory_mean <- trajectory_data |>
  filter(is.finite(log_gfp)) |>
  group_by(year_bs) |>
  summarise(
    mean_log_gfp = mean(log_gfp),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ggplot(
  trajectory_data,
  aes(
    x = year_bs,
    y = log_gfp,
    group = hhid
  )
) +
  geom_line(
    color = "grey65",
    alpha = 0.7,
    na.rm = TRUE
  ) +
  geom_point(
    color = "grey65",
    alpha = 0.7,
    na.rm = TRUE
  ) +
  geom_line(
    data = trajectory_mean,
    aes(
      x = year_bs,
      y = mean_log_gfp,
      group = 1
    ),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    color = "black",
    linewidth = 1.2
  ) +
  geom_point(
    data = trajectory_mean,
    aes(x = year_bs, y = mean_log_gfp),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    color = "black",

  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2064:2072) +
  labs(
    title = "Provisional GFP trajectories for selected households",
    subtitle = "Grey: households; black: selected-household annual mean",
    x = "Nepali year (BS)",
    y = "log(1 + provisional GFP)"
  ) +

```

#### iv. Plot subgroup proportions
```{r}
# One pooled threshold, held fixed across all years
gfp_threshold <- quantile(
  analysis_data$gfp_preview[
    is.finite(analysis_data$gfp_preview)
  ],
  probs = 0.75,
  names = FALSE
)

subgroup_data <- analysis_data |>
  mutate(
    above_threshold = case_when(
      !is.finite(gfp_preview) ~ NA_real_,
      gfp_preview > gfp_threshold ~ 1,
      TRUE ~ 0
    )
  ) |>
  filter(
    !is.na(ethnic),
    !is.na(above_threshold)
  ) |>
  group_by(ethnic, year_bs) |>
  summarise(
    n_observed = n(),
    proportion = mean(above_threshold),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ggplot(
  subgroup_data,
  aes(
    x = year_bs,
    y = proportion,
    color = ethnic,
    group = ethnic
  )
) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2064:2072) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = scales::percent,
    limits = c(0, 1)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Proportion above a fixed provisional GFP threshold",
    subtitle = paste(
      "Threshold: pooled 75th percentile =",
      round(gfp_threshold, 2),
      "(mixed units)"
    ),
    x = "Nepali year (BS)",
    y = "Proportion among observed households in each group",
    color = "Ethnicity"
  ) +
  theme_bw()

```


### B. Run model
#### i. Mutli-level for continuous outcome
```{r}
# Basic time model
ml_full <- lme(
  fixed = log_gfp ~ time,
  random = ~ 1 + time | hhid,
  # The residuals of the same family are calculated using AR(1), retaining the real year intervals
  correlation = corAR1(
    value = 0.2,
    form = ~ time | hhid,
    fixed = FALSE
  ),

  data = model_data,
  method = "REML",
  na.action = na.fail,

  control = lmeControl(
    opt = "nlminb",
    maxIter = 100,
    msMaxIter = 300,
    msMaxEval = 1000
  )
)

summary(ml_full)
VarCorr(ml_full)
coef(
  ml_full$modelStruct$corStruct,
  unconstrained = FALSE
)
```


```{r}
# remove the random time slope and retain AR(1)
ml_reduced <- NULL

ml_reduced <- lme(
  fixed = log_gfp ~ time,

  random = ~ 1 | hhid,

  correlation = corAR1(
    value = 0.2,
    form = ~ time | hhid,
    fixed = FALSE
  ),

  data = model_data,
  method = "REML",
  na.action = na.fail,

  control = lmeControl(
    opt = "nlminb",
    maxIter = 100,
    msMaxIter = 300,
    msMaxEval = 1000
  )
)

summary(ml_reduced)

# Compare model fitting
# The two models use the same samples, fixed effects and AR(1) structure
stopifnot(nobs(ml_full) == nobs(ml_reduced))

kable(
  AIC(ml_reduced, ml_full),
  digits = 2,
  caption = "Random intercept versus random intercept and slope"
)

# Calculate the likelihood ratio test statistic
lrt_stat <- 2 * (
  as.numeric(logLik(ml_full)) -
    as.numeric(logLik(ml_reduced))
)

if (lrt_stat < -0.001) {
  stop("Full model has lower likelihood. Check optimization.")
}

lrt_stat <- max(0, lrt_stat)

# Calculate the P-value using an approximate mixed distribution
mixture_p <- 0.5 * pchisq(
  lrt_stat, df = 1, lower.tail = FALSE
) +
  0.5 * pchisq(
    lrt_stat, df = 2, lower.tail = FALSE
  )

# Use formatted text to avoid very small P-values being displayed as 0
kable(
  data.frame(
    LRT = round(lrt_stat, 3),
    p_value = format.pval(
      mixture_p,
      digits = 3,
      eps = 0.0001
    )
  ),
  caption = "Approximate test of random time-slope variance"
)
```
We compared a random-intercept model with a random-intercept and random-slope model, retaining an AR(1) residual correlation structure in both. Adding a random time slope improved model fit (AIC: 62036.34 versus 61993.68; approximate likelihood ratio test: 46.657, p < 0.0001). This supports allowing the linear time trend to vary across households. We therefore retain the random-intercept and random-slope structure with AR(1) residuals for the next modeling step. These findings remain preliminary because the GFP composite combines different units and component availability differs across years.

```{r}
ml_main <- update(
  ml_full,
  fixed = log_gfp ~ time +
    log_rem +
    farm_tech +
    log_labor +
    log_land_c,
  data = model_data,
  method = "REML"
)

summary(ml_main)
VarCorr(ml_main)
coef(
  ml_main$modelStruct$corStruct,
  unconstrained = FALSE
)
```
The adjusted multilevel model included remittances, farm technology, hired labor, and average land ownership, together with time. Random household intercepts, random time slopes, and AR(1) residual correlation were retained. Remittances showed a small positive association with the log-transformed provisional GFP composite (β = 0.0093, p = 0.0292). Farm technology, hired labor, and average land ownership were also positively associated with the outcome (all p < 0.0001), while the time coefficient was negative (β = −0.1580, p < 0.0001). The estimated AR(1) parameter was 0.575. These associations remain preliminary because the outcome combines different units and the availability of its components varies across years.

```{r}
ml_time_ML <- update(
  ml_full,
  method = "ML"
)

ml_main_ML <- update(
  ml_main,
  method = "ML"
)

stopifnot(
  nobs(ml_time_ML) == nobs(ml_main_ML)
)

anova(ml_time_ML, ml_main_ML)
```
Using maximum likelihood estimation, we compared the time-only model with a model additionally including remittances, farm technology, hired labor, and average land ownership. Both models retained random household intercepts, random time slopes, and AR(1) residual correlation. Adding the four predictors significantly improved model fit (likelihood ratio test: χ²(4) = 1238.68, p < 0.0001). AIC decreased from 61983.50 to 60752.82, and BIC decreased from 62036.15 to 60835.56. We retain the adjusted model for further diagnostics, with substantive interpretation remaining provisional because of unresolved outcome measurement issues.

```{r}
# Extract the standardized residuals after considering the relevant structures, as well as the fitted values at the household level
res_main <- residuals(ml_main, type = "normalized")
fit_main <- fitted(ml_main, level = 1)

old_par <- par(mfrow = c(1, 2))

# Check whether the residuals take on a curve or funnel shape with the fitted values
plot(
  fit_main, res_main,
  xlab = "Fitted values",
  ylab = "Normalized residuals",
  main = "Residuals vs fitted",
  pch = 16,
  cex = 0.4,
  col = adjustcolor("steelblue", alpha.f = 0.25)
)
abline(h = 0, col = "red", lty = 2)

# Check whether the residual distribution is close to normal
qqnorm(
  res_main,
  main = "Normal Q-Q plot",
  pch = 16,
  cex = 0.4
)
qqline(res_main, col = "red")

par(old_par)
```

```{r}
diag_data <- nlme::getData(ml_main)
stopifnot(nrow(diag_data) == length(res_main))
diag_data$normalized_residual <- as.numeric(res_main)

# Residual distribution in each year
boxplot(
  normalized_residual ~ year_bs,
  data = diag_data,
  xlab = "Nepali year (BS)",
  ylab = "Normalized residuals",
  main = "Residuals by year",
  col = "lightblue",
  outline = FALSE
)

abline(h = 0, col = "red", lty = 2)
```

Keep the original model and fit another one that does not include the year 2072:
```{r}
# Sensitivity analysis data
model_data_pre72 <- model_data |>
  filter(year_bs < 2072) |>
  droplevels()

ml_main_pre72 <- update(
  ml_main,
  data = model_data_pre72,
  method = "REML"
)

# Compare the coefficient and standard error
full_results <- summary(ml_main)$tTable
pre72_results <- summary(ml_main_pre72)$tTable

comparison <- data.frame(
  term = rownames(full_results),
  estimate_all_years = full_results[, "Value"],
  SE_all_years = full_results[, "Std.Error"],
  estimate_without_2072 =
    pre72_results[rownames(full_results), "Value"],
  SE_without_2072 =
    pre72_results[rownames(full_results), "Std.Error"],
  row.names = NULL
)

kable(
  comparison,
  digits = 4,
  caption = "Sensitivity analysis: including versus excluding 2072"
)
```
The sensitivity analysis showed that the estimates were sensitive to the inclusion of 2072. Excluding this year reversed the signs of both the time coefficient (−0.1580 to 0.0462) and the remittance coefficient (0.0093 to −0.0081). Farm technology, hired labor, and average land ownership remained positively associated with the outcome, although their estimated coefficients changed. Thus, the direction of the remittance association was not robust to the analysis period. Given the reduced availability of GFP components in 2072, both specifications are retained as preliminary analyses pending further assessment of measurement comparability.

```{r}
# Residual diagnosis excluding the 2072 model
res_pre72 <- residuals(
  ml_main_pre72,
  type = "normalized"
)

fit_pre72 <- fitted(ml_main_pre72, level = 1)

old_par <- par(mfrow = c(1, 2))

plot(
  fit_pre72, res_pre72,
  xlab = "Fitted values",
  ylab = "Normalized residuals",
  main = "Residuals: 2064–2071",
  pch = 16,
  cex = 0.4,
  col = adjustcolor("steelblue", alpha.f = 0.25)
)
abline(h = 0, col = "red", lty = 2)

qqnorm(
  res_pre72,
  main = "Normal Q-Q: 2064–2071",
  pch = 16,
  cex = 0.4
)
qqline(res_pre72, col = "red")

par(old_par)
```
Excluding 2072 did not resolve the residual diagnostic concerns. The residual-versus-fitted plot continued to show structured patterns and uneven dispersion, while the normal Q-Q plot showed substantial departures from normality in both tails. Thus, the model adequacy concerns are not confined to 2072. Together with the reversal of the time and remittance coefficients in the sensitivity analysis, these findings indicate that substantive conclusions remain tentative. Further assessment of outcome construction, missing-data handling, and model specification is needed.
